North Shore surf report: a big swell arrives

By Kai Makoa · October 11, 2026

A long-period swell from the north-west reached the North Shore overnight, with sets of 12 to 15 feet by mid-morning. Lifeguards closed several beaches and asked inexperienced surfers to stay out of the water.

Conditions

  • Swell: north-west, 14 seconds
  • Wind: light trade winds, offshore until noon
  • Tide: high at 06:12, low at 12:31

Spot by spot

SpotSizeCrowd
Pipeline12–15 ftHeavy
Sunset Beach10–12 ftModerate
Waimea Bay15+ ftLight

Safety

  1. Check with the lifeguards before paddling out.
  2. Never surf alone in a swell like this.
  3. Read our guide to big waves.

“It’s the best start to a season in ten years,” said one lifeguard.

The swell is expected to ease on Monday. See the full forecast.
